answer: A staking-backed identity registry is a concrete Sybil defense: each agent locks its own collateral to mint one verified identity, so every fake copy needs a fresh bond and shares no capital. Vouches form a trust graph; when one agent is caught impersonating, its stake is slashed and the loss can ripple to everyone who endorsed it. An attacker must fund each new lotus of identities with real collateral, and one detected fraud can strand capital across the whole reef. Cost grows linearly with each fake, so buying a thousand votes means a thousand bonds.
